# IngrediLens

> IngrediLens is an iPhone and iPad app that reads the ingredient list on food and cosmetic labels and highlights the allergens and ingredients you chose to avoid, including “may contain” warnings. It reads labels in English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French and Italian, works without an account, and keeps your data on your device. It is free to download, with an optional Premium subscription.

Key facts: iPhone and iPad (iOS / iPadOS 17+). Free download with 2 filters; optional Premium subscription (monthly with 3-day free trial, yearly with 7-day free trial). No account; data stays on the device; no ads or tracking. Reads labels in English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French and Italian; free restaurant allergy card in 15 languages. Built-in database of more than 24,000 ingredients with cited sources (EU Regulations 1169/2011, 1223/2009, 1333/2008, CosIng, US FDA FALCPA/FASTER Act). Not a medical device: it never says a product is safe, cannot detect cross-contact, and users must always read the pack. Developer: Enescan İşler (independent). Current version 1.4 (28 October 2026). Contact: enescanisler@icloud.com

- About / fact page (canonical facts, method, sources): https://ingredilensapp.com/about/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6806595642
- Support and FAQ: https://ingredilensapp.com/
- Privacy policy: https://ingredilensapp.com/privacy.html
- Full version of this file: https://ingredilensapp.com/llms-full.txt

## Guides (English)

- [All guides (hub)](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/): food allergy and label guides in English, Español, Português, Deutsch, Français, Italiano
- [How to read allergen labels on food (EU, UK and US)](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/how-to-read-allergen-labels/): In the EU and UK, allergens are part of the ingredients list and must be emphasised, usually in bold.
- [What does "may contain" mean on food labels?](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/may-contain-traces-meaning/): “May contain” and “traces of” warn about possible cross-contact: the allergen is not in the recipe but could get into the product during production.
- [The 14 EU allergens list, explained with examples](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/eu-14-allergens-list/): EU and UK law (Annex II of Regulation 1169/2011) lists 14 allergens that must be emphasised in the ingredients list: cereals containing gluten, crustaceans, eggs, fish, peanuts, soybeans, milk, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites, lupin and molluscs.
- [The 9 major food allergens in the US (FALCPA and sesame)](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/us-major-food-allergens/): US food labels must declare nine major allergens: milk, egg, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans and sesame, which was added from 1 January 2023 by the FASTER Act.
- [E-numbers explained, what the codes on food labels mean](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/e-numbers-explained/): E-numbers are codes for food additives authorised in the EU, such as E330 for citric acid; the label shows the additive’s function followed by its name or E-number.
- [Hidden gluten on food labels, names to look for](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/hidden-gluten-names/): Gluten is in wheat (including spelt, durum, semolina and khorasan), barley, rye and foods made from them, such as malt, bulgur, couscous and seitan.
- [Hidden milk on labels, other names for dairy](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/hidden-milk-names/): Milk can appear as casein, caseinates, whey, lactose, ghee, butter, cream, curd or milk solids.
- [Hidden egg on food labels, other names for egg](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/hidden-egg-names/): Egg can appear on labels as albumen or albumin, ovalbumin, ovomucoid, lysozyme (E1105), egg lecithin or dried egg.
- [Hidden soy on food labels, other names for soya](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/hidden-soy-names/): Soy can appear as soya, soy lecithin (E322), edamame, miso, tempeh, tofu, textured vegetable protein (TVP) or hydrolysed soy protein, and on cosmetics as Glycine Soja.
- [Hidden peanut and tree nut names on food labels](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/hidden-peanut-tree-nut-names/): Peanuts are legumes and tree nuts are a separate allergen group, so labels and allergists treat them separately.
- [Sesame, mustard, celery and lupin, the overlooked allergens](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/sesame-mustard-celery-lupin/): Sesame, mustard, celery and lupin are on the EU’s list of 14 allergens and often hide in tahini, spice mixes, stock cubes, sauces and gluten-free flours.
- [Travelling with food allergies, restaurant allergy cards](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/restaurant-allergy-card-travel/): Before a trip with a food allergy, update your plan with your doctor, pack your adrenaline auto-injectors and learn the local words for your allergens and “may contain”.
- [Eating out with coeliac disease, a practical guide](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/eating-out-coeliac-disease/): With coeliac disease even small amounts of gluten matter, so eating out depends on how the kitchen avoids cross-contamination.
- [Food allergies at school and childcare, what to give carers](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/food-allergy-school-plan/): Give the school, nursery or carer an allergy action plan completed with your child’s doctor, in-date adrenaline auto-injectors if prescribed, and a clear list of the foods to avoid with their other names.
- [Reading cosmetic INCI ingredient lists for sensitive skin](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/cosmetic-ingredients-sensitive-skin/): Cosmetic ingredients are listed by INCI name in descending order of amount, with ingredients under 1% in any order at the end.
- [How to choose an allergen scanner app, a checklist](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/allergen-scanner-app-checklist/): Allergen scanner apps either look up a barcode in a database or read the ingredient list printed on the pack.
- [How to keep a food reaction diary to find triggers](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/food-reaction-diary/): A reaction diary records what you ate or used, when symptoms started, what they were and how bad they were, plus foods you tolerated.
- [Allergy and ingredient scanner apps compared](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/allergy-scanner-apps-compared/): Scanner apps fall into four groups: barcode scorers (such as Yuka), diet and allergy filters (such as Fig), cosmetic ingredient apps (such as INCI Beauty and Think Dirty) and label readers (such as IngrediLens).
- [IngrediLens: questions and answers](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/ingredilens-faq/): IngrediLens reads food and cosmetic ingredient lists with the iPhone camera, a photo, typed text or a barcode, and highlights the allergens you choose plus "may contain" statements.
- [Yuka alternative for food allergies: what to use](https://ingredilensapp.com/guides/en/yuka-alternative-food-allergies/): Yuka rates the overall health impact of food and cosmetics, which is useful for healthier shopping.

## Free tools

- [Free restaurant allergy card (15 languages)](https://ingredilensapp.com/allergy-card/): Make, print or save a card that explains your food allergies to restaurant staff abroad.
- [Ingredient list allergen checker](https://ingredilensapp.com/ingredient-checker/): Paste an ingredient list and see which of your allergens and “may contain” warnings it mentions.
- Allergy card in other languages: [Español](https://ingredilensapp.com/es/tarjeta-de-alergias/), [Português](https://ingredilensapp.com/pt/cartao-de-alergia/), [Deutsch](https://ingredilensapp.com/de/allergiekarte/), [Français](https://ingredilensapp.com/fr/carte-allergies/), [Italiano](https://ingredilensapp.com/it/scheda-allergie/)

## Reference

# Pawfood

> Pawfood is an iPhone app that scans dog and cat food labels and checks the ingredients against your pet's allergies and avoid list. It reads a barcode or a photo of the ingredient list (also on iPad) and matches every ingredient against the allergens, suspected sensitivities and avoid items the owner records for each pet. It explains vague terms such as "poultry" or "animal fat", compares foods on a dry matter basis and keeps a food journal. Privacy: pets, scans and journal stay on the device; no account, no ads, no tracking; buying or restoring Pawfood Plus sends an anonymous purchase record (random ID, no personal or pet data) to RevenueCat.

Key facts: iOS / iPadOS app, App Store https://apps.apple.com/app/id6831189714. Languages: English, Turkish, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, German, French. Free download with 3 scans; result status and allergen matches are always shown and brand recall notices are always free; optional Pawfood Plus subscription (Premium or Family, monthly or yearly, yearly with a 3-day free trial) adds unlimited scans, full ingredient breakdown with dry matter and carbohydrate estimates, comparison of up to 4 foods, food journal with vet report PDF. Four result states: "Match found", "Worth a closer look", "No recorded match" (never a safety statement), "Not enough data". Knowledge base: 767 ingredients, 76 allergen families, 14 species notes, editorial draft not reviewed by a veterinarian, sourced from AAFCO, FEDIAF, EU feed law, U.S. FDA, WSAVA, Merck Veterinary Manual and peer-reviewed papers. Not a veterinary service: no diagnosis or treatment. Product data: Open Pet Food Facts (ODbL); recall data: openFDA. Publisher: Opsis Digital, support@opsisdigital.com.

- Home page: https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/ (also https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/, https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/es/, https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/pt-br/, https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/de/, https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/fr/)
- Ingredient explanations (EN): https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/ingredients/ · (TR): https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/ingredients/
- Dry matter calculator: https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tools/dry-matter-calculator/ · (TR): https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/tools/dry-matter-calculator/
- Guides: https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/ · Allergen families: https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/
- Privacy policy: https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/privacy.html · Terms: https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/terms.html

## Pawfood guides (English)

- [Food allergy or food intolerance? How they differ in dogs and cats](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/allergy-vs-intolerance/): Food allergy involves the immune system; intolerance doesn't. Signs overlap, so only a vet-led elimination trial can tell them apart. What to know and note.
- [\"Poultry\", \"animal fat\", \"natural flavor\": vague pet food label terms explained](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/ambiguous-terms-poultry/): Which pet food label terms don't name the animal, what each one can contain, why it matters for allergy lists, and how to get a straight answer from the manufacturer.
- [What "by-product" and "meal" really mean on a pet food label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/by-products-and-meals/): By-products and meals are defined feed terms, not insults. Learn what they include, why the species name matters and how to read them for allergies.
- [Most commonly reported food allergens in cats, and where they hide on labels](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/common-cat-food-allergens/): Beef, fish and chicken top the published cat cases. What the numbers mean, why they aren't a risk ranking, and where those proteins hide on cat food labels.
- [Dry matter basis explained: how to compare wet and dry pet food](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/dry-matter-basis/): What dry matter is, how to convert a guaranteed analysis step by step, how to estimate carbohydrates honestly, and the mistakes that make comparisons misleading.
- [Keeping a pet food journal: what to record and how to share it with your vet](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/food-journal-guide/): A practical guide to logging foods, treats, symptoms, stool and weight in a way your vet can use, without reading too much into the patterns yourself.
- [Grain-free pet food: what the label means and what it doesn't](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/grain-free-explained/): Grain-free means no cereal grains; it isn't a low-carb or allergy claim. What replaces grains, and what the FDA said about diet and DCM.
- [How to read a dog or cat food label, step by step](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/how-to-read-pet-food-labels/): A practical walk through every part of a pet food label: product name rules, ingredient order, guaranteed analysis, the adequacy statement, feeding guide and the small print.
- [Hydrolyzed protein diets: how they work and what the label tells you](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/hydrolyzed-protein-diets/): Hydrolysis breaks proteins into small pieces the immune system is less likely to recognize. Less likely is not never: what studies found, what to ask.
- [Preservatives in pet food: mixed tocopherols, BHA, BHT and ethoxyquin](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/preservatives-explained/): A neutral look at why pet foods contain preservatives, how natural and synthetic antioxidants differ, what the rules say and how to read them on a label.
- [Puppy and kitten food labels: growth, all life stages and large breeds](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/puppy-kitten-food-labels/): What to check on a puppy or kitten food label, from the growth statement and the large-breed wording to calories, calcium and feeding guides.
- [Senior pet food labels: what "senior" does and doesn't tell you](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/senior-pet-food-labels/): There is no separate legal standard for senior pet food. Learn what to check on the label instead, from calories and protein to joint claims and missing values.
- [How treats and toppers can undo an allergy diet](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/treats-and-toppers/): Treats, chews, toppers and flavoured extras often carry the very proteins a diet avoids. Here is how to check them and keep a diet trial consistent.
- [Wet vs dry pet food: how to compare the labels fairly](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/guides/wet-vs-dry-food-labels/): Wet food looks low in protein because it is mostly water. Learn to compare canned and dry labels on a dry matter and calorie basis, step by step.

## Pawfood guides (Türkçe)

- [Mama alerjisi mi, intolerans mı? Kedi ve köpeklerde fark](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/allergy-vs-intolerance/): Mama alerjisinde bağışıklık sistemi devrededir, intoleransta değil. Belirtiler benzediği için ayrımı veteriner kontrolünde eliminasyon denemesi yapar.
- [\"Kanatlı\", \"hayvansal yağ\", \"doğal aroma\": mama etiketindeki belirsiz terimler](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/belirsiz-terimler-kanatli-hayvansal-yag/): Hangi mama etiketi terimleri hayvanın adını vermez, her biri neyi içerebilir, alerji listeleri için neden önemlidir ve üreticiden net yanıt nasıl alınır.
- [Mama etiketinde "yan ürün" ve "un" gerçekte ne anlama gelir](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/by-products-and-meals/): Yan ürün ve un tanımlı yem terimleridir, hakaret değil. Neleri kapsadıklarını, hayvan adının neden önemli olduğunu ve alerji açısından nasıl okunacağını öğren.
- [Kedilerde en sık bildirilen mama alerjenleri ve etikette nerede saklandıkları](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/common-cat-food-allergens/): Yayımlanmış kedi vakalarında sığır eti, balık ve tavuk başı çekiyor. Rakamlar ne anlatır, neden risk sıralaması değildir, bu proteinler etikette nerede gizlenir?
- [Kuru madde nedir, nasıl hesaplanır: yaş ve kuru mamayı karşılaştırmak](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/kuru-madde-nedir-nasil-hesaplanir/): Kuru maddenin ne olduğu, analitik bileşenlerin adım adım nasıl çevrileceği, karbonhidratın dürüstçe nasıl tahmin edileceği ve karşılaştırmayı yanıltan hatalar.
- [Mama günlüğü tutmak: ne kaydetmeli, veterinerle nasıl paylaşmalı](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/food-journal-guide/): Mamayı, ödülleri, belirtileri, dışkıyı ve kiloyu veterinerinin kullanabileceği şekilde kaydetmek için pratik bir rehber; örüntüleri tek başına yorumlamadan.
- [Tahılsız mama: etiket ne söyler, ne söylemez](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/grain-free-explained/): Tahılsız, mamada tahıl olmadığını söyler; düşük karbonhidrat ya da alerji iddiası değildir. Yerine ne konur ve FDA'nın DCM incelemesi neler söyledi?
- [Kedi ve köpek maması etiketi adım adım nasıl okunur](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/mama-etiketi-nasil-okunur/): Mama etiketinin her bölümünü pratik olarak anlatır: ürün adı kuralları, içerik sırası, analitik bileşenler, yeterlilik beyanı, besleme önerisi ve küçük yazılar.
- [Hidrolize protein diyetleri: nasıl çalışır, etiket ne söyler?](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/hydrolyzed-protein-diets/): Hidroliz proteini küçük parçalara ayırır; bağışıklık sisteminin onu tanıma ihtimali azalır ama sıfırlanmaz. Çalışmalar ne buldu, veterinerine ne sormalısın?
- [Mamalarda koruyucular: karışık tokoferoller, BHA, BHT ve etoksikin](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/preservatives-explained/): Mamalarda neden koruyucu bulunduğuna, doğal ve sentetik antioksidanların farkına, kuralların ne dediğine ve etikette nasıl okunacağına tarafsız bir bakış.
- [Yavru köpek ve yavru kedi maması etiketi: büyüme, tüm yaşam evreleri ve büyük ırklar](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/puppy-kitten-food-labels/): Yavru köpek ya da yavru kedi maması etiketinde nelere bakmalı: büyüme beyanı, büyük ırk ifadesi, kalori, kalsiyum ve besleme önerisi.
- [Yaşlı hayvan maması etiketi: "yaşlı" ne söyler, ne söylemez](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/senior-pet-food-labels/): Yaşlı hayvan maması için ayrı bir yasal standart yok. Etikette onun yerine nelere bakacağını öğren: kalori, protein, eklem iddiaları ve eksik değerler.
- [Ödül mamaları ve mama üstü katkılar alerji diyetini nasıl bozar](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/treats-and-toppers/): Ödül mamaları, çiğneme ürünleri, mama üstü katkılar ve aromalı ekstralar çoğu zaman diyetin kaçındığı proteinleri taşır. Nasıl kontrol edeceğini öğren.
- [Yaş mama mı, kuru mama mı: etiketleri adil karşılaştırmak](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/tr/guides/wet-vs-dry-food-labels/): Yaş mamada protein düşük görünür, çünkü büyük kısmı sudur. Konserve ve kuru mama etiketlerini kuru madde ve kalori bazında adım adım karşılaştır.

## Pawfood allergen families

- [Barley on pet food labels — pearled barley, malt, barley grass and brewers yeast](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/barley/): How barley appears on cat and dog food labels, why malt and brewers yeast deserve a look, and how Pawfood flags barley and unclear grain terms.
- [Beef allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/beef/): Beef allergy in dogs and cats: every label name for beef and veal, vague meat terms, tallow and gelatin, chews and a label checklist.
- [Bison allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/bison/): Bison allergy or avoidance in dogs and cats: KB label names for bison, why bison recipes may hold other meats, and a label checklist.
- [Chicken allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/chicken/): Chicken allergy in dogs and cats: every label name for chicken, vague terms like poultry, fat and hydrolyzed forms, and a label checklist.
- [Corn (maize) on pet food labels — names, by-products and what to check](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/corn/): Corn appears on pet food labels as meal, gluten meal, bran, starch, oil and more. See every name, the unclear terms and how Pawfood flags them.
- [Dairy allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/dairy/): Dairy allergy in dogs and cats: every label name for milk, whey, casein, cheese and yogurt, lactose, goat milk and a label checklist.
- [Duck allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/duck/): Duck allergy in dogs and cats: every label name for duck, duck fat in other recipes, vague poultry terms and a label checklist.
- [Egg allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/egg/): Egg allergy in dogs and cats: every label name for egg, yolk, egg white and dried egg, eggshell membrane, lecithin and a label checklist.
- [Fish allergy in dogs and cats: salmon, whitefish, tuna and more on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/fish/): Fish allergy in dogs and cats: KB names for salmon, whitefish, tuna, sardine and other fish, fish oil, vague seafood terms and a checklist.
- [Gluten grains on pet food labels — wheat, barley, rye and unclear terms](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/gluten/): Which pet food ingredients count as gluten grains (wheat, barley, rye), which are only possible matches, and why oats and starches need a closer look.
- [Goat allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/goat/): Goat meat allergy or avoidance in dogs and cats: KB label names for goat, why goat milk is listed under dairy, vague terms and a checklist.
- [Horse allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/horse/): Horse meat allergy or avoidance in dogs and cats: KB label names for horse, vague meat terms on EU labels, and a label checklist.
- [Insect protein allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/insect/): Insect protein allergy or avoidance in dogs and cats: KB names for black soldier fly larvae, mealworm and cricket, and a label checklist.
- [Kangaroo allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/kangaroo/): Kangaroo allergy or avoidance in dogs and cats: KB label names for kangaroo, why novel-protein recipes still need checking, and a checklist.
- [Lamb and mutton allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/lamb/): Lamb allergy in dogs and cats: every label name for lamb and mutton, vague meat terms, lamb fat, chews and a label checklist.
- [Oats on pet food labels — oatmeal, oat bran, oat fiber and cat grass](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/oat/): How oats appear on cat and dog food labels, what oat fiber and cat grass are, why oats and gluten are linked, and how Pawfood flags them.
- [Peas on pet food labels — pea protein, starch, fiber and split names](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/pea/): Peas appear on pet food labels as whole peas, pea protein, starch and fiber, often several times in one list. See every name and how Pawfood flags them.
- [Pork allergy in dogs and cats: what to check on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/pork/): Pork allergy in dogs and cats: every label name for pork and wild boar, gelatin and plasma, pig ears and skins, vague terms and a checklist.
- [Potato on pet food labels — dried potato, starch, protein and fiber](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/potato/): How potato appears on cat and dog food labels, from dried potato to potato starch and protein, which terms are unclear, and how Pawfood flags them.
- [Poultry allergy in dogs and cats: chicken, turkey, duck and other birds on the label](https://isler404.github.io/apps/pawfood/allergies/poultry/): Avoiding all poultry for a dog or cat? Every KB name for chicken, turkey, duck, goose, quail and generic poultry, plus vague terms and a label checklist.
